title: autotune: default batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Singh
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching and KV caching heuristics, introduces pre-baked quantization profiles for common family/seqlen combinations, and ships a lightweight unit-economics CLI and console card to surface per-route token cost and suggested config changes. Backwards compatible defaults; opt-in rollout flag for sensitive customers.
description: Summary: Implements the first integrated rollout of autotune defaults: adaptive batching and prefix/KV caching defaults, curated quantization profiles, and a unit-economics (uecon) tooling surface. Motivation: customers repeatedly run into high per-token costs and manual tuning for batching/caching/quantization. This PR automates sensible defaults and provides visibility/actions so teams can achieve unit-econ improvements without deep runtime tuning. Changes: (1) Autotune engine: new heuristics that pick default batch windows and cache TTL based on observed request size/arrival distributions and latency SLO. (2) Quantization profiles: ship a config table of tested profiles (int8/int4 variants + kernel hints) keyed by model family and typical sequence length buckets. (3) Unit-econ tooling: a CLI and Console card that shows per-route cost breakdown (tokens, model variant, batch efficiency) and generates suggested config patches (batch_window/cache_ttl/quant_profile). (4) Telemetry and dashboards: new metrics (uecon_cost_per_req, batch_fill_ratio, cache_hit_ratio) and Grafana dashboard. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `autotune.defaults.v1`; staged canary for 10% traffic -> 50% -> global with rollback hooks. Backwards compatibility: defaults are opt-in and can be pinned per-customer; no model weight changes performed by the runtime. Tests: unit + integration tests added for heuristics; performance bench using perf-canary included with representative workloads. Perf results: in internal canary we saw median token cost reduction of 18% (95% CI: 14-22%) for chat-like workloads and 12% latency change at p50 (within SLO). Security/ops: added audit logs for automated config changes and KMS-safe markers for quant artifacts. Documentation: cost-optimization.md and quickstart updated. See commits and changed files for details.

notes_on_testing: Added deterministic unit tests for heuristic boundaries, mocked arrival trace integration tests, and an internal perf-canary run with chat, completion, and embedding workloads. Bench harness and scripts included under ci/perf/harness/.
observability_changes: Introduces metrics: uecon_cost_per_req, batch_fill_ratio, cache_hit_ratio; adds Grafana dashboard JSON and alert thresholds for batch_fill_ratio < 0.3 and cache_hit_ratio < 0.2.
rollout_plan: Feature flagged behind runtime config `autotune.defaults.v1`. Canary rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 24h evaluation windows. Auto rollback if uecon_cost_per_req increases by >5% for two consecutive windows or latency breaches SLO.
manual_steps_for_ops: To enable for a customer: set runtime flag, monitor uecon metrics, optionally pin quant_profile via /v1/deployments/:id/config. CLI `tools/uecon/cli.py diff --route <route>` shows suggested patches.
